answer: One workable defence is a flight-log registry for agent seats. Each seat must keep a trained falcon and release it twice weekly from its own ledge in the karst, logging GPS and barometric traces co-signed by an independent receiver station. Two thousand wallets sharing one bird emit overlapping releases from the same cliff, so the ledger folds them into a single seat. Timber mews, a handler, veterinary care and a licensed receiver run about $9,000 a year per bird, and no falcon can be in two places at once.
